scope: Generated conservative recognition from the actual Linux/session dispatch arms
Unimplemented syscall completion on the calling worker
Original policy, diagnostic log and legacy/tracing boundaries
implementation: One shared macro emits unchanged dispatcher expressions and number recognition; numeric guards remain conservative and pure dynamic predicates are reused
AIO before the main tables uses its original aio_call predicate; future pre-dispatch families must expose/reuse their entry predicate
Cold source completion returns ENOSYS only when neither dispatch table nor AIO owns the entry
Already handled hot calls bypass the classifier; seccomp decisions, TRAP/termination and explicit tracing keep their original entry handling
Retained original log/PID/bounded command name produces the same diagnostic without retaining VFS/Process/Files or guest pointers
constraints: No new coordinator/service thread or polling bus
No new ordinary guest-byte synchronization or access policy
Existing errno and guest diagnostic semantics preserved
Same runtime on Mac/iPad; Dev-only deployment

performance.source_note: Final production code was used for all valid guest runs. Subsequent changes only add test assertions, documentation and paired version metadata. The installed metadata build has separate smoke acceptance.

performance_interpretation: Three alternating unprofiled pairs per CPU count/mode. Timed short runs use 1000 calls per thread; long denied-only controls use 100000. Thread creation, ready barrier and optional TSYNC precede the timed release.
Unknown calls rotate through 16 numbers at/above 0xff00, use invalid pointer-shaped arguments, and must return ENOSYS or the accepted seccomp ERRNO42 without reading those arguments.
Raw and ALLOW unknown calls gain by removing repeated whole-cohort returns. This does not predict Firefox/Geekbench performance or represent all known-but-unsupported subcommands.

Short ERRNO controls regress by approximately 0.9 ms at four CPUs and 3.3 ms at twelve CPUs. Long-run medians regress by approximately 2% at four/twelve CPUs and 5% at one CPU; the one-CPU outlier is preserved. Zero overhead is not claimed.
The fixed-latency cause remains unattributed. No classifier was added to the early denial path; scheduling/initial memory publication and code layout are hypotheses, not proven causes.

Native reference is an ARM64 Linux CI guest with six provisioned CPUs; twelve threads are oversubscribed and no CPU pinning is used. Native Linux does not emit the same per-call guest diagnostic, while Trames preserves its existing bounded/rate-limited log.
The earlier measurement overlapping compilation is retained separately; reported short medians use the subsequent idle run. The long denied-control run was also separate.
Diagnostic samples have no tested unknown or set_robust_list cohort returns. Other console/memory/control boundaries and some aggregate service requests remain.
corrected_failures: The existing profile test expected unknown numbers to return the cohort; update that expectation and retain a known membarrier entry plus an explicit tracing case as positive controls
An initial benchmark script referenced the old fixture filename and ran no valid benchmark; corrected before collecting the reported data
The root boundary check requires committed clean runtime state; its pre-commit attempt failed that gate and the paired clean check passed
validation_reuse: Both full runtime workflows and both 396-case process suites passed. Afterward only tracing/legacy test assertions and documentation changed; corresponding final targeted checks passed on both hosts. Existing product/HVF, instruction/graphics and prior Go/Docker acceptance are reused rather than claimed as freshly rerun. The complete dispatch body audit preserves nonseparator tokens/strings/guards, except the equivalent credential prelude moved into the first dynamic arm.
physical_ipad_acceptance: Device/simulator compile checks only; no new physical iPad deployment.
known_unattributed_issues: Short denied-call fixed-latency regression described above
Earlier stage-56 intermittent Docker cleanup timeout remains unattributed; no new Firefox or Docker acceptance claimed
remaining_boundaries: Known handler resources/subcommands that refuse source admission
Actual host lifecycle/admin and exceptional native/memory publication
Explicit tracing and diagnostic-less legacy embeddings
Unhandled HLT/fault/backend exits and cold/solo orchestration
